# COR021 `pointer-initialisation-in-declaration`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A procedure's local pointer is initialised in its declaration (`=> null()`), which implies `save`.

## Why

Pointer initialisation in a declaration gives the pointer the SAVE attribute: after the first call
it keeps whatever association the previous call left, possibly to deallocated memory. Nullify it
with an executable statement instead.

## Reported

```fortran
real, pointer :: p(:) => null()
```

## Preferred

```fortran
real, pointer :: p(:)
nullify(p)
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR021] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR021` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C082` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
